ratings.comment: Please stay away from this guy.

I had Prof. D. for J335 and J559 this semester. The 559 power lectures felt like the longest hours of my life. Tests were more about application than memorization, but homework prepares you for them. In 335 we didn't do much; it was an easy A but I'd recommend someone else. Grading wasn't very clear and we didn't have a structured syllabus.

Lectures seemed to be about 7 hours long, but the material is actually pretty interesting, if you can stay awake. Drechsel wasn't particularly helpful outside of class, but is there if you need something. Tests were pretty hard, but if you go to class and do the readings, no reason you shouldn't pass.

Prof D--as he likes to call himself--was a great professor. I had minimal out-of-class interaction with him but when I did, he was a very nice man. J559 was advanced and extremely difficult. There is a lot of material but he teaches you exactly what he wants you to know. Exams were more about applying what you learned than spitting it back out.

Highly recommend him--very nice guy, pretty interesting, engaging content/class structure. 675 is pure discussion, no textbook, just select readings. Grade is 10 *short* essays, and one bigger paper--no tests. Good sense of humor and a really nice, smart guy, I'd definitely take it.

One of the best courses I have taken at UW-Madison thus far in my college career. Professor Drechsel provides students with the tools to apply knowledge about Media Law to a wide variety of situations and contexts. Coming out of the class, I feel that I have gain knowledge that will help me in the future. He has a great sense of humor.

The class can get a bit dry, but I think that's to be expected with the subject matter. Drechsel tries to keep class fun with his examples, and he's very knowledgable. That said, tests are fairly demanding so study a LOT and memorize necessary precedent and tests.

He is very down to earth and interesting in class. Doesn't have the arrogance of normal professors. I've heard he gets a little restless during office hours, but I've never been so I can't speak for myself.
